subject: Agriculture
title: Shuttle Breeding
description: A fast breakdown of Shuttle Breeding for builders.

hook.text: Borlaug grew wheat in two locations per year—winter in one, summer in another. Other breeders called him crazy.

buildup.text: Conventional breeding grew one generation per year. Shuttle breeding between sites doubled the pace.

discovery.text: Growing in different environments accidentally selected for adaptability. His wheat worked in diverse climates.

twist.text: The establishment resisted. Textbooks said shuttle breeding shouldn't work. Borlaug ignored the textbooks.

climax.text: In 10 years, Borlaug achieved what traditional methods would need 20. Speed saved millions of lives.

punchline.text: Break the rules, breed twice as fast, feed the world.

quiz.question: What was controversial about Borlaug's shuttle breeding?
options: He grew two generations per year against conventional wisdom
